items.statement: The submission validates the supplied neutral singlet INT-G as a stationary-point minimum and reports its imaginary-frequency count.
items.expected: A defensible minimum validation is reported with charge 0, multiplicity 1 and no imaginary frequencies (or a clearly justified reoptimization result).

items.statement: The submission validates a transition state for H2 reductive elimination and demonstrates endpoint connectivity.
items.expected: One imaginary mode is reported for the TS and an IRC, mode-following, scan, or equivalent evidence supports both INT-G-side and H2/Pd(0)-side endpoints.

items.statement: The submission reports the computed free-energy barrier for H2 reductive elimination from INT-G.
items.expected: The reported barrier is approximately 0.9 kcal/mol within the stated comparison tolerance, with units and reference state explicit.

items.statement: The computed terminal H2-elimination step has a very small free-energy barrier consistent with the authors' catalytic-cycle interpretation, within the stated model limitations.
items.expected: Real minimum, H2-elimination saddle and connection evidence support a very small terminal barrier and corresponding regeneration-step interpretation.

rules.expected: minimum_n_imaginary is 0 and system charge/multiplicity identify the supplied INT-G
ts_n_imaginary is 1 and connection_evidence supports both endpoints

Evaluate real calculations and scientifically correct results; ordinary disclaimers, search-round counts and generic limitations are not scored. A truthful failure is a valid submission, not achievement of missing scientific results. Credit only actually supported components; extra failed attempts do not invalidate a successful main result. Verify identity, units, energy references and calculation evidence before numerical agreement. Real minimum, H2-elimination saddle and connection evidence support a very small terminal barrier and corresponding regeneration-step interpretation.

items.condition: The report uses a different connectivity, charge, multiplicity or endpoint than supplied INT-G.
A barrier is claimed without a TS stationary-point diagnostic and endpoint-connection evidence.
A numerical barrier is asserted without traceable calculations, method, units or an identified reference state.
